questions.q: According to the summary, why does direct instruction fail to teach young children?
a: It treats children as passive objects to be told what to know
It gives children too much freedom to choose their activities
It relies on play instead of structured lessons
It asks children to learn skills before they know any facts
questions.why: Lesson 1 says direct instruction is passive, assumes students are objects, and so does not work.

questions.q: Why did preschools shift toward lecturing instead of play, according to lesson 1?
a: Parents' high expectations and safety worries shaped the system
Studies proved that lectures helped children remember more
Teachers were trained to avoid unstructured classroom time
Children asked for quieter lessons where they could sit still
questions.why: Lesson 1 says anxious parents pushed schools to look safer and more academic, which meant more lecturing.

questions.q: What does the summary say play does for a child's development?
a: It builds memory and other essential cognitive functions
It burns off energy so children can sit still afterward
It teaches children to compete for a teacher's attention
It removes the need for a trusting bond with adults
questions.why: Lesson 2 says play has a vital role, including building memory and other cognitive abilities.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest a teacher respond when a child asks a question?
a: Let the class work together to find the answer
Answer it quickly so the lesson stays on schedule
Write it down for the children to research at home
Explain that the class will cover it in a later year
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes letting kids lead a group search for a solution, including one they raised themselves.

questions.q: What change does the summary recommend for school curriculums?
a: Replace useless facts with skills like problem-solving
Add more tests to measure what children have learned
Start formal lectures at an earlier age
Shorten the school day so children can rest more
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the curriculum should drop useless facts and teach skills children can use in school and life.
